links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading level of chatbot responses to patient questions
links.effect: GPT-3.5 Flesch-Kincaid score 18.3 versus GPT-4 15.4 (significantly higher for GPT-3.5), indicating difficult reading level in both.
links.quote: On the Flesch- Kincaid scale, GPT-3.5 responses had a significantly higher score of 18.3 compared to GPT-4's 15.4, indicating a more difficult reading level in GPT-3.5's responses.

links.outcome: Evidence-based support rating of chatbot responses by surgeons
links.effect: Both ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 scored lowest on the evidence-based criterion; overall averages 19.7/25 (GPT-3.5) and 18.7/25 (GPT-4).
links.quote: Both models scored lowest on "Evidence-based" prompts.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 answering patient-facing clinical questions regarding glenohumeral osteoarthritis, assessed by expert clinicians for accuracy, readability, and reliability without testing an organizational deployment safeguard.
